System Architecture & Functional Requirements

The Modnote application was engineered as a high-performance CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) system tailored for academic data management. The technical requirements focused on data persistence and UI responsiveness:

  • WinForms Desktop Environment: Developed within the .NET ecosystem to exploit native Windows API hooks for superior memory management and window handle efficiency.
  • Automated ETL (Extract, Transform, Load): Implemented a data-parsing layer that extracts metadata from external source files to dynamically instantiate module objects, including assessment timelines and learning KPIs.
  • Rich-Media Persistence: Engineered a note-taking engine capable of serialising and de-serialising complex data types (RTF, Bitmaps, and URIs) while maintaining relational integrity with parent modules.
  • State-Driven Display Logic: Utilised conditional rendering to switch between collective dashboard views and granular, tab-indexed module environments.

UX Engineering & Interaction Design

  1. User Workflow Heuristics:

    • Applied a "Shortest Path" architectural model to minimise the depth of the navigation tree.
    • Conducted task-flow analysis to ensure core academic functions—such as cross-referencing learning outcomes during note creation—required zero context switching.

  2. Responsive Component Design:

    • Developed custom layout anchors and autoscaling logic within the Windows Forms designer to ensure UI consistency across varying DPI settings and desktop resolutions.
    • Established a strict visual hierarchy using typographic scale and "negative space" to mitigate information density issues common in enterprise-style software.

  3. Interaction & Affordance:

    • Integrated tab-controlled containers and dropdown enumerations to maintain "Information Scent," providing clear visual affordance for module selection.
    • Engineered an asynchronous drag-and-drop interface for note reordering, utilising event-handling to update the underlying data collection in real-time.

  4. Inclusive System Design:

    • Validated colour palettes against WCAG luminosity ratios to ensure high-readability for users with visual impairments.
    • Implemented a comprehensive Keyboard Focus Map (Tab-Indexing) and mnemonic hotkeys for high-speed, mouse-less interaction.

Full-Stack Development Highlights

  • C# .NET Implementation: Utilised Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) principles, specifically Encapsulation and Inheritance, to build modular C# classes for "Module" and "Note" entities.
  • Stream I/O & File Handling: Developed a resilient file-system watcher and stream-reader to automate the ingestion of academic data, incorporating try-catch blocks for robust error-handling of corrupted input strings.
  • GDI+ & Rich Text Processing: Leveraged GDI+ for rendering embedded media and custom-built RTF logic to support advanced text formatting and hyperlink injection within the note-keeping interface.
  • Data Structure Optimisation: Employed generic collections (List, Dictionary<TKey, TValue>) for efficient data retrieval, ensuring O(1) or O(n) complexity when searching through large volumes of academic content.

Key Technical Outcomes

  • Optimised Information Throughput: The system successfully reduced the overhead of academic file management, allowing for immediate retrieval of associated assessment data via linked module IDs.
  • Full-Lifecycle Engineering: Managed the complete SDLC (Software Development Life Cycle), translating high-level UX requirements into a functional C# codebase.
  • Robust UI Performance: Achieved zero-latency rendering for complex note blocks by optimising the underlying GDI+ drawing calls and event-loop prioritisation.
  • Scalable Architecture: Built a modular foundation that allows for future expansion into SQL database integration or cloud-based data synchronisation.

childMarkdownRemark.html:
ModNote is a desktop application designed to help users manage academic modules and their associated notes effectively. Built using Windows Forms in C#, this project highlights the seamless integration of user experience (UX), design, and development.

The application meets essential user needs by offering an intuitive interface for managing module information, creating detailed notes, and organising content—all optimised specifically for desktop use.
